Let a status stand once it is reached

Source: R/carry_status.R
carry_status.Rd

The fix for the transitions ensure_transitions() forbids, when you know which status holds: a completed education stays completed, the highest education completed never falls. The status is carried forward over the unit's later observations, and the earlier, wrong ones after it are overwritten in a new column. Once the rule is given there is one right result, so the function does not guess, as merge_spells() does not.

Usage

carry_status(data, id, time, status, final = NULL, order = NULL, name = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, or a database or Arrow table: see Database and Arrow tables in checkpoints.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr.

time

The period column, or the start of a spell (one column).

status

The status column (one column).

final

Statuses that hold once reached.

order

All statuses, from lowest to highest.

name

Name of the column for the result. Defaults to the status column's name followed by _carried.

Value

data with the carried status in the column name: a tibble for a data frame, in the original row order, or a query for a database or Arrow table.

Details

Two ways to give the rule, one operation:

  • final: once a unit reaches one of these statuses, it holds in every later observation. With several, the first one reached holds.

  • order: the statuses from lowest to highest; a unit's status is the highest it has had so far, so it never goes back in the order. Every status in the data must be in order.

Later observations are taken in time order, whatever the distance, as in describe_transitions(). A missing status after the status is reached gets it too; one before keeps its missing value. Rows with a missing time are left as they are.

The fix is never silent: it says how many rows and units it changed, counted per change, such as not started -> completed: 37 rows in 31 units. The result goes to a new column by default, so the original status stands beside it and the changed rows can be found by comparing the two; numbers behind a published table should not change without a trace of where. Give name = <the status column> to overwrite it.

The unit is what the id columns say. Carried per person, a completed education overwrites the start of the next one; carry per person and education, id = c(cpr, education).

See also

ensure_transitions() and describe_transitions() to find the transitions first.

Examples

education <- data.frame(
  cpr    = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b"),
  year   = c(2019, 2020, 2021, 2019, 2020, 2021),
  status = c("enrolled", "completed", "enrolled",
             "not started", "enrolled", "completed")
)
carry_status(education, cpr, year, status, final = "completed")
#> ℹ Changed 1 row in 1 unit:
#>   enrolled -> completed: 1 row in 1 unit
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   cpr    year status      status_carried
#>   <chr> <dbl> <chr>       <chr>         
#> 1 a      2019 enrolled    enrolled      
#> 2 a      2020 completed   completed     
#> 3 a      2021 enrolled    completed     
#> 4 b      2019 not started not started   
#> 5 b      2020 enrolled    enrolled      
#> 6 b      2021 completed   completed     

# The highest level so far
levels <- data.frame(cpr = "a", year = 2019:2022, level = c(1, 3, 2, 4))
carry_status(levels, cpr, year, level, order = 1:4)
#> ℹ Changed 1 row in 1 unit:
#>   2 -> 3: 1 row in 1 unit
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   cpr    year level level_carried
#>   <chr> <int> <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1 a      2019     1             1
#> 2 a      2020     3             3
#> 3 a      2021     2             3
#> 4 a      2022     4             4
